title: Cylinder
spec: To construct the cylindrical base, start by creating a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to zero and a translation vector also set to zero. In the first face, draw the first loop consisting of four lines. The first line runs from the origin (0.0, 0.0) to (0.0197, 0.0). The second line extends from (0.0197, 0.0) to (0.0197, 0.0197). The third line moves from (0.0197, 0.0197) to (0.0, 0.0197), and the fourth line completes the loop by connecting (0.0, 0.0197) back to the origin. Apply a scale factor of 0.0197 to the entire sketch to ensure uniform dimensions. Transform the scaled sketch into three-dimensional space by rotating it with Euler angles set to zero and translating it with a vector of zeros. Extrude the sketch 0.75 units along the normal direction to create a solid body. This operation should result in a cylindrical object with a sharp, pointed tip at one end and a flat, circular base at the other. The cylinder has a consistent diameter throughout its length, measuring 0.019736842105263153 units in both width and height, and 0.7499999999999999 units in length.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Create a sketch on the XY plane
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0197, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0197, 0.0197) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.0197) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch to create a cylinder
r = r.extrude(0.75)

# The final model is represented as 'r'
